skill.name: create-auth-skill
skill.description: Scaffold and implement authentication in TypeScript and JavaScript apps using Better Auth. Detect frameworks, configure database adapters, set up route handlers, add OAuth providers, and create auth UI pages.
skill.summary: Guides Better Auth setup across JavaScript frameworks, database adapters, route handlers, OAuth providers, plugins, and auth pages.
skill.author: better-auth

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around filenames, package names, imports, documentation links, and placeholder environment variables. I confirmed the package manager and migration command guidance as real external-command risk because it can install packages or alter schema state after user approval. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Package and CLI commands can modify the user project.
remediation.suggestion: Show each npm, npx, Prisma, or Drizzle command to the user and require explicit confirmation before execution.

remediation.issue: Database migration commands can change schema state.
remediation.suggestion: Generate migration files for review when possible, avoid automatic production migrations, and recommend a database backup first.

remediation.issue: The skill discusses secrets and database connection strings.
remediation.suggestion: Keep all values as placeholders, never print secrets, and remind users to keep environment files out of commits.

| Next.js App Router | `app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts` | `toNextJsHandler(auth)` → export `{ GET, P
**Next.js Server Components:** Add `nextCookies()` plugin to auth config.
| Prisma | `npx @better-auth/cli@latest generate --output prisma/schema.prisma` then `npx prisma mig
**Session check (client):** `useSession()` hook returns `{ data: session, isPending }`
**Protected routes:** Check session, redirect to `/sign-in` if null.

content.value_statement: Adding secure authentication to JavaScript apps requires framework, database, route, and provider choices. This skill guides Better Auth setup from planning through migration, UI, and production checks.
actual_capabilities: Detects framework, database, ORM, existing auth library, and package manager cues.
Guides structured planning questions before implementation starts.
Maps Better Auth server, client, route handler, adapter, and plugin setup.
Provides migration commands for Kysely, Prisma, and Drizzle workflows.
Covers auth UI flows, protected routes, sessions, and troubleshooting.
Includes a security checklist for secrets, cookies, origins, rate limits, and CSRF.
limitations: Requires user confirmation before implementation and migrations.
Focuses on TypeScript and JavaScript projects that can use Better Auth.
Does not provide a complete generated application by itself.
External CLI and package commands should be reviewed before execution.

use_cases.title: Add Auth To A New App
use_cases.description: Plan and scaffold Better Auth for a new Next.js, SvelteKit, Express, or Hono project.

use_cases.title: Migrate From An Auth Library
use_cases.description: Audit an existing auth setup and plan an incremental Better Auth migration.

use_cases.title: Configure Enterprise Features
use_cases.description: Add OAuth, 2FA, organizations, admin controls, bearer tokens, or SSO with matching plugins.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Better Auth Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan Better Auth for my project. Detect my framework, database, auth needs, and package manager before changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Add Email And OAuth
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add email and password plus Google or GitHub sign-in to this app. Ask required planning questions first.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Database Migrations
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to configure Better Auth with my ORM and prepare migrations. Show every command before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate Existing Auth
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my current auth implementation and create an incremental migration plan to Better Auth with rollback checkpoints.

output_examples.input: User asks to add sign-in and sign-up to an existing Next.js app.
output_examples.output: The skill reports detected Next.js App Router, asks about database and providers, then returns a checklist for dependencies, server config, route handler, and pages.

output_examples.input: User wants Prisma with Google OAuth and 2FA.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes Better Auth packages, Prisma adapter setup, OAuth secret requirements, plugin choices, migrations, and production security checks.

output_examples.input: User is migrating from another auth library.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines audit steps, parallel setup, route migration, session replacement, UI updates, old library removal, and testing points.

best_practices: Confirm the implementation plan before editing files or running commands.
Review generated migrations and back up databases before applying changes.
Keep secrets in environment variables and out of commits or logs.
anti_patterns: Running package manager or migration commands without user approval.
Adding OAuth providers before redirect URLs and secrets are ready.
Disabling CSRF, secure cookies, or origin checks to bypass errors.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps plan and implement Better Auth login, sign-up, sessions, providers, plugins, and auth pages.

faq.question: Which frameworks can it guide?
faq.answer: It covers Next.js, SvelteKit, Nuxt, Astro, Express, Hono, SolidStart, Vue, React, and vanilla JavaScript clients.

faq.question: Does it create database migrations?
faq.answer: It guides migration commands for Better Auth, Prisma, and Drizzle. Review generated changes before applying them.

faq.question: Can it help with OAuth providers?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks which providers are needed and lists the required client IDs, secrets, and callback setup.

faq.question: Does it include production security checks?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers secrets, secure cookies, trusted origins, rate limits, email verification, CSRF protection, and account linking review.

faq.question: Should commands run automatically?
faq.answer: No. Package installation and migration commands should be shown and confirmed before execution.
